purpose: Close ASVS V6.3.7 for the credential-reset path by queueing the already-written but never-called passwordChangedMail security notice through the existing durable auth-mail outbox, inside the same transaction that replaces the password. Before this change the notice was never sent: the template had zero call sites anywhere in apps/ or packages/, and confirm() only returned a notificationDelivery field in its HTTP response, leaving actual delivery to whoever called it.
requiredInvariants: No database migration: the PASSWORD_CHANGED mail kind is already permitted both by AUTH_MAIL_KINDS in auth-mail-outbox.service.ts and by the auth_mail_outbox_kind_check constraint in migration 20260812010000_p0_industrial_auth_mail_outbox.

The notice is enqueued inside the same transaction as the password replacement, so a committed reset cannot leave the account holder unnotified and a rolled-back reset cannot queue a notice for a change that did not happen.
The enqueue idempotency key is derived from the reset challenge id, so a retried confirmation reuses the queued notice rather than sending a second one.

The deliveryAuthorized() server-to-server boundary is left exactly as it is. Relaxing it changes who may complete a reset at all and is a separate owner decision, not a side effect of this notification fix.
The confirm() response shape is unchanged, so the existing server-to-server consumer keeps working.
No security control is weakened; this scope adds a control that was absent.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation.

docs/security/cryptographic-inventory.json/CRYPTOGRAPHIC_INVENTORY.md are regenerated via scripts/security/discover-cryptography.mjs only (no hand edits) - the added randomUUID() correlation-id call changes the tracked UUID call-site count that the exact-match test in discover-cryptography.test.mjs checks.
acceptance: passwordChangedMail has a real runtime call site: password-reset.service.ts confirm() enqueues kind PASSWORD_CHANGED through AuthMailOutboxService.
pnpm --filter @pc/api typecheck passes with zero errors.
password-reset.service.spec.ts covers both directions: the notice is queued once with a challenge-keyed idempotency key on a completed reset, and is not queued at all when the reset fails.
The full src/modules/auth suite passes with no regressions.
